title: Unit 3 Mixed Review Core Test
description: Review slope, y-intercept, linear equations, graphing, and multiple representations of lines.

questions.questionText: A line passes through (-4, 0) and (-2, -1). What is its slope?
questions.explanation: Slope is change in y divided by change in x.

questions.questionText: In y = 5/2x - 1, what is the y-intercept?
questions.explanation: In y = mx + b, the y-intercept is b.

questions.questionText: Which equation has slope 3/5 and y-intercept -7?
questions.explanation: Put the slope in the m position and the y-intercept in the b position.

questions.questionText: A line has equation y = 6/5x + 5. Which graphing description is correct?
questions.explanation: Graph by starting at the y-intercept and using slope as rise over run.

questions.questionText: A table includes -4 -> 6, -2 -> 5, 0 -> 4. Which equation matches it?
questions.explanation: The table has constant rate m and starting value b.

questions.questionText: A line contains (0, 9) and (5, 43/2). Which equation represents the line?
questions.explanation: The point with x = 0 gives b, and the second point confirms the slope.

questions.questionText: Which point is the y-intercept of y = 3/5x - 4?
questions.explanation: The y-intercept is always on the y-axis, so x = 0.

questions.questionText: A line starts at -5 and changes by 6/5 each step. What is the value when x = 16?
questions.explanation: Substitute x into y = mx + b.

questions.questionText: Two representations show slopes -1/2 and 1/2. Which has the greater rate of change?
questions.explanation: Compare the slope values; the greater slope is the greater rate of change.

questions.questionText: A student says y = 5/2x has slope 0. What is the student's mistake?
options: They used the reciprocal of the slope
They changed the sign of every y-value
They confused the y-intercept with the slope
questions.correctAnswer: They confused the y-intercept with the slope
questions.explanation: In y = mx + b, m is the slope and b is the y-intercept.

questions.questionText: A line has slope 3/5 and passes through (3, 19/5). What is its y-intercept?
questions.explanation: Use y = mx + b with the given point, then solve for b.

questions.questionText: Which statement best explains why slope is constant on a line?
options: Any two slope triangles on the line have the same rise/run ratio
The run is always 1 for every line
The y-intercept changes each time x changes
Every line must pass through the origin
questions.correctAnswer: Any two slope triangles on the line have the same rise/run ratio
questions.explanation: Slope triangles on the same line are similar, so their rise/run ratios match.
